resources.string: You control start and stop recording.
Recordings are automatically started and stopped
Take a photo when a trigger occurs. Video recording stays manual.
Add your first trigger to capture the good stuff: a 5% descent above 50 km/h, or your next 500 W+ burst.
Choose a ride event or threshold to capture moments automatically. You can add several triggers.
Capture a moment whenever Karoo records a new lap.
Capture your hard efforts when power crosses your chosen wattage.
Capture fast stretches when speed crosses your chosen threshold.
Capture the summit of a climb on your active route.
Capture intense efforts when heart rate crosses your chosen threshold.

This trigger uses the selected automation mode during an active ride. Threshold triggers fire once on crossing, then rearm after you fall below the reset boundary. Missing sensor data cannot trigger a capture.
Ride boundaries only add highlights to a video already recording. They never start a video or take a photo. Pausing and resuming do not add boundary markers.

Choose one mode and add triggers. Only add automatic highlights keeps video start and stop under your control. Auto recording starts a video on a trigger and, by default, stops it after all enabled thresholds have been inactive for a full minute. A new effort or event resets that delay. You can change the delay or turn automatic stopping off in Auto recording settings. Automatic highlights are on by default. Only take photos automatically captures one still per event, with at least 30 seconds between photos; it skips busy, recording or disconnected cameras. Events are never saved for later. Manual recordings are never stopped automatically. Pausing or finishing a ride, changing automation settings, or losing the camera connection returns any current clip to manual control. Missing sensor data pauses the stop timer until fresh data is available. The camera must be on and connected.
